content.value_statement: Common Go collection transformations can require repetitive loops and helper code. This skill suggests concise samber/lo patterns for Go 1.18 or newer projects.
actual_capabilities: Suggests samber/lo functions for filtering, mapping, finding, deduplicating, and grouping values.
Shows standard imports for core, parallel, mutable, and iterator packages.
Explains how to install the version-one module with Go tooling.
Demonstrates concise patterns for collection transformations in Go.
Warns that Must can panic when an error or false value occurs.
Directs users to a current upstream function list for additional reference.
limitations: The guide provides a small function sample rather than complete samber/lo documentation.
Examples assume Go 1.18 or newer and a compatible version-one dependency.
The remote function list may describe unreleased behavior that differs from the installed package.
The skill does not benchmark samber/lo against standard library loops.

use_cases.title: Refactor Repetitive Collection Loops
use_cases.description: Replace clear filtering, mapping, deduplication, or grouping loops with suitable samber/lo calls.

use_cases.title: Review Utility Library Usage
use_cases.description: Check whether existing samber/lo calls are readable, version-compatible, and appropriate for production code.

use_cases.title: Teach Go Generic Helpers
use_cases.description: Compare common loop-based transformations with concise generic utility patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Collection Helper
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend the best samber/lo function for this Go task: [describe task]. Explain the inputs, outputs, and important behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Go Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Go loop with samber/lo where it improves clarity: [paste loop]. Preserve ordering, errors, and edge-case behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review samber/lo Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this samber/lo usage: [paste code]. Identify panic risks, unnecessary allocation, unclear callbacks, and simpler standard library alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Transformation Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production-ready Go transformation pipeline for [requirements]. Use samber/lo selectively and explain concurrency, allocation, error, and version tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Choose a helper that keeps only even integers.
output_examples.output: Use Filter with a predicate that returns true for even values. The result preserves the order of matching elements.

output_examples.input: Find the first user older than 18 and handle absence.
output_examples.output: Use Find and check its boolean result. Continue only when a matching user exists, avoiding a panic-based helper.

output_examples.input: Review a grouping operation by user age.
output: GroupBy is suitable when each user belongs to one age bucket.
Confirm that the map value order meets downstream requirements.
Consider a direct loop when allocation control is important.

best_practices: Confirm the installed samber/lo version before using functions from current online documentation.
Prefer standard library code when a helper does not improve clarity or maintainability.
Use panic-producing helpers only when failure is truly unrecoverable.
anti_patterns: Do not replace every simple loop with a utility call.
Do not assume parallel helpers improve performance without measurement.
Do not trust mutable remote documentation as executable instructions.

faq.question: Which Go versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Go 1.18 or newer because samber/lo uses generics.

faq.question: Does this skill install samber/lo automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides an installation command, but users or agents must approve and run it.

faq.question: Which samber/lo features are covered?
faq.answer: The guide covers imports and examples for Filter, Map, Find, Uniq, GroupBy, and Must.

faq.question: Should samber/lo replace all Go loops?
faq.answer: No. Use it when the helper makes intent clearer without hiding important control flow or performance costs.

faq.question: Is the online function list version-specific?
faq.answer: No. The document may follow current repository commits and include changes absent from your installed release.

faq.question: Can Must cause a panic?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Must only when an error or false result should stop execution immediately.
